exposure: large-for-gestational age (LGA) diagnosed during second-trimester ultrasound examination
cohort: The cohort included pregnant women who underwent a second-trimester anatomy ultrasound examination between 18 and 22 weeks, excluding those with a history of pre-GDM, multiple gestation, preterm delivery, betamethasone use, or fetal anomaly.
finding: Large-for-gestational age (LGA) diagnosed during the second-trimester ultrasound examination is significantly associated with the development of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and LGA at birth, independent of known risk factors.
birth_weight: LGA at birth defined as birth weight >= 90th percentile; appropriate-for-gestational age (AGA) at birth defined as estimated fetal weight > 10th percentile and <= 89th percentile.
gest_age: Second-trimester ultrasound examinations performed between 18 and 22 weeks gestational age; LGA and AGA definitions were percentile-based for gestational age.
